$comment: Data acquisition map for 'Dancing with the SARs' (NASA Space Apps 2026, Cochabamba). Built 2026-11-14 from the challenge Resources tab and the ASF NISAR Data User Guide. Hand this file to the download agent. Never put credentials in this file.

project.name: Dancing with the SARs
project.local_theme: Alerta Temprana de Riesgos en Cuencas (early warning for river-basin risks: floods, mudflows/torrents, slope instability, soil saturation)
project.goal: Track and visualize surface change over the Cochabamba basin with NISAR L-band SAR (water/flooding, soil moisture, vegetation change, ground deformation) and present it in an interactive web app.

basin.name: Full basin extent (union of GAMC 'Cuencas UH 7' and 'Cuencas UH 8')

area_of_interest.notes: Use 'basin' for searches and clipping; use 'core_city' for the default app view. The Tunari range (north) drains through torrents into the Rocha river valley: slope deformation and mudflow risk are in the north, flooding in the valley floor.

time_windows.seasonality: Cochabamba rainy season is roughly December-March; dry season roughly May-October. Comparing dry vs. wet acquisitions is the core change-detection story.

nisar_availability.BETA: Subset of acquisitions 2025-10-17 to 2026-01-20 (up to 8 per track). Not calibrated. May or may not cover Cochabamba: check first.
nisar_availability.PROVISIONAL: All L-band acquisitions 2026-06-17 to ~2026-10-23 (dry season). Calibrated, partially validated.
nisar_availability.VALIDATED: All L-band acquisitions from 2026-10-21 onward. Fully calibrated and validated (L0-L2). SME2 not yet validated.

recommended.purpose: Start of rainy season; keep pulling new acquisitions as they arrive (12-day repeat)
Optional: previous rainy season, only if it covers the AOI. Do not mix quantitatively with PROVISIONAL/VALIDATED without flagging it.

time_windows.caution: Differences between BETA, PROVISIONAL and VALIDATED products can come from processing changes (different CRID), not real surface change. Label the maturity of every layer shown in the app.

earthdata_login.how: Read credentials from environment variables EARTHDATA_USERNAME / EARTHDATA_PASSWORD, or from a ~/.netrc (Windows: %USERPROFILE%\_netrc) entry for machine urs.earthdata.nasa.gov. earthaccess.login() picks up either automatically.
earthdata_login.rule: Ask the user for credentials at runtime or use the env/netrc. Never write them into code, this file, logs or the repo.

gamc_wms.how: Project API key from https://recursosgamc.cochabamba.bo/api-doc (project 02). Store it as GAMC_WMS_KEY in the backend .env only.
gamc_wms.rule: The key travels in the URL: proxy it through our backend, never expose it in the frontend or commit it.

tips: NISAR files are HDF5 and large (GCOV hundreds of MB to GB; RSLC ~30 GB). Prefer streaming + subsetting to the AOI over full downloads.
Stream with earthaccess.open(results) or fsspec HTTPS (cache_type='background', block_size=16MB) and xarray.open_datatree(engine='h5netcdf', phony_dims='access', decode_timedelta=False).
GDAL /vsicurl/ can subset HDF5 without downloading the whole file.
Direct S3 access only works from AWS us-west-2; from a laptop use HTTPS.

datasets.name: NISAR L2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV)
datasets.why: Main layer. Radiometrically terrain-corrected L-band backscatter (gamma0). Water and flooded areas appear dark (specular); HV tracks vegetation volume; time series show soil wetting, flooding and vegetation loss. Directly answers 'which polarizations highlight the change'.
selection_rules: Keep ONE track/frame geometry (same relative orbit, same direction) for the time series so pixels are comparable; record track and frame from the file name (NISAR_L_L2_PR_GCOV_CYL_REL_P_FRM_...).
If both ascending and descending cover the AOI, pick the one with more acquisitions; optionally keep the other as a second series.
Take every available date in each window (12-day repeat).
datasets.pixel_spacing: 10 or 20 m (frequency A), 80 m (frequency B); UTM projection
datasets.output: Clip to basin bbox, convert to dB, write one Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF per date and polarization (EPSG:3857 or keep UTM + overviews), plus a Zarr cube (time, y, x) per polarization for animations and pixel time series.

datasets.name: NISAR L2 Geocoded Unwrapped Interferogram (GUNW)
datasets.why: Centimetre-scale ground displacement: slope movement on the Tunari foothills (landslide/mudflow precursors) and valley subsidence. Coherence loss also flags surface disturbance after storms.
subset_layers: connected components / mask (exact HDF5 paths: inspect one file first and record them here)
selection_rules: Prefer consecutive 12-day pairs (sequential network) for a displacement time series; keep pair dates in metadata.
datasets.output: Line-of-sight displacement (mm) and coherence as COGs per pair, clipped to basin.

datasets.name: NISAR L3 Soil Moisture (SME2)
datasets.why: Ready-made soil moisture: saturated soils plus rain means runoff and flood risk. Only PROVISIONAL exists so far (VALIDATED expected 2027).
datasets.notes: Check spatial resolution and AOI coverage before committing to it. If it doesn't cover the basin, derive a relative wetness index from GCOV instead.

datasets.name: OPERA L2 RTC from Sentinel-1 (C-band)
datasets.why: Multi-year history (2016+) to show past rainy seasons and flood events that NISAR missed; C-band vs L-band comparison is something the challenge explicitly suggests (different frequencies).
datasets.notes: Verify the short name and AOI coverage in Earthdata Search before bulk download. Pick 2-3 wet-season peaks (Jan-Mar) and matching dry-season dates.

datasets.name: OPERA L3 Dynamic Surface Water Extent from Sentinel-1 (DSWx-S1)
datasets.why: Ready-made water masks to validate our NISAR water/flood thresholds.
datasets.notes: Verify short name and coverage (South America) before use.

datasets.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30
datasets.why: Same DEM family NISAR uses for terrain correction. Needed for slope, flow direction, drainage and the 3D terrain view in the app.
datasets.source: AWS Open Data: s3://copernicus-dem-30m/ (public, no auth; tiles named Copernicus_DSM_COG_10_S18_00_W067_00_DEM etc.) or OpenTopography.
datasets.tiles_needed: Tiles covering lat -18 to -17, lon -67 to -65 (S18 W067, S18 W066, plus neighbours if the basin bbox crosses them).
datasets.output: Mosaic, clip to basin, COG + terrain-RGB tiles (for MapLibre/deck.gl terrain) + slope COG.

datasets.name: GPM IMERG Final Daily precipitation
datasets.why: Rain is the driver. Plot rainfall next to SAR backscatter/soil wetness so the app can explain why the surface changed.
datasets.notes: Verify current version/short name in Earthdata Search. Extract a daily time series for the basin (mean over bbox) covering 2025-10-01 to today. Final runs lag ~3.5 months: use GPM_3IMERGDL (Late) for the most recent weeks.
datasets.output: CSV/Parquet: date, precip_mm (basin mean), plus optional small daily grid as Zarr.

datasets.name: Optical context: Harmonized Landsat Sentinel-2 (HLS) or Sentinel-2 L2A
datasets.why: Human-readable context next to radar (true colour, NDVI) for storytelling; cloud-free dates only.
datasets.notes: Optional. Pick 1 clear dry-season date and 1 wet-season date closest to SAR acquisitions.

datasets.name: GAMC municipal WMS layers (Cochabamba)
datasets.why: Local ground truth: basins, drainage, emergency records, district boundaries, 2750 m contour (urban growth limit).
datasets.access: WMS 1.1.1 via proxy https://serviciosgamc.cochabamba.bo/api/gs/wms with params key, service_id, SERVICE=WMS, VERSION=1.1.1 (GetLegendGraphic 1.0.0), REQUEST, LAYERS= (empty). Operations: GetMap (PNG), GetLegendGraphic (PNG), GetFeatureInfo (application/json).
datasets.download: Not downloadable as vectors: consume live through the backend proxy; GetFeatureInfo for attributes on click.

services.name: Limite Distritos
services.note: Portal lists this with the same bbox as Cota 2750 (likely an error); bbox here taken from the same layer in project 03.

datasets.name: JRC Global Surface Water (occurrence)
datasets.why: Permanent vs. seasonal water reference (Laguna Alalay, reservoirs) so the app doesn't flag permanent water as floods.

download_plan: 1. Authenticate with earthaccess.login() (env vars or netrc). Stop and ask the user if credentials are missing.

2. Search nisar_gcov for all maturities over area_of_interest.basin; write a manifest (granule name, date, track, frame, direction, maturity, size, URL) to data/manifests/nisar_gcov.csv BEFORE downloading anything.
3. Choose the track/frame per nisar_gcov.selection_rules and report the choice plus total size to the user.
4. Stream/subset the chosen GCOV granules to the basin and the listed layers; save intermediates under data/raw/ (never commit).
5. Repeat steps 2-4 for nisar_gunw (same track/frame), then nisar_sme2 if it covers the AOI.
6. Download Copernicus DEM tiles and GPM IMERG daily series.
8. Convert outputs to COG / Zarr / CSV under data/processed/ following each dataset's 'output'.

storage_layout.data/manifests/: Search results as CSV (small, can be shared)
storage_layout.data/raw/: Original or subset HDF5/GeoTIFF/NetCDF (large, never commit)

rules_for_agent: Do not commit or push anything to git.
Do not store credentials anywhere in files.
Show the manifest and estimated total size to the user before any download larger than ~5 GB.
Mark any short name flagged 'verify' as confirmed or corrected in your report.
